cable-triceps-pushdown.description: A standing cable extension that trains the triceps through a direct downward press with a straight bar.
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley, take an overhand grip, and stand with your elbows tucked beside your ribs.
Press the bar down by straightening your elbows while keeping your shoulders and upper arms still.
Finish with the bar near your thighs, then let it rise under control until your forearms approach your upper arms.
Keep your wrists stacked over the bar and avoid leaning onto it or letting your elbows drift forward.

rope-triceps-pushdown.description: A rope-based cable extension that allows the hands to separate as the elbows reach full extension.
instructions: Clip a rope to a high pulley, grasp an end in each hand, and set your elbows close to your sides with a neutral grip.
Drive the rope downward by extending your elbows, separating the ends as they pass your hips.
Reach a firm straight-arm finish, then guide the rope upward until your elbows are fully bent without moving your upper arms.
Keep your torso quiet and do not turn the movement into a shoulder pull or wrist flick.

reverse-grip-triceps-pushdown.description: An underhand cable pushdown that challenges triceps control while the forearms stabilize the bar.
instructions: Set a straight bar on a high pulley and hold it palms up with your elbows pinned near your waist.
Extend your elbows to draw the bar toward your thighs, keeping the underhand grip and upper arms fixed.
Pause with your arms straight, then allow the bar to return smoothly until your forearms near your biceps.
Keep your wrists neutral and use a secure grip so the bar does not roll into your fingers.

single-arm-cable-pushdown.description: A unilateral cable extension that lets each triceps work independently through a downward pressing path.
instructions: Attach a single handle to a high pulley, face the stack, and hold the handle with one elbow tucked against your side.
Press the handle down by extending only the working elbow while keeping your chest square to the cable.
Finish with the hand beside your thigh, then return the handle slowly to the fully bent-elbow position before switching arms.
Keep the working shoulder level and resist twisting or using your body to drive the handle.

overhead-cable-triceps-extension.description: A standing cable extension performed overhead to train the triceps with the arms beside the head.
instructions: Attach a rope to a low pulley, face away from the stack, and bring the rope overhead with your elbows pointing forward.
Extend your elbows to send the rope forward and upward while your upper arms stay close to your ears.
Separate the rope ends at full extension, then bend your elbows slowly to bring your hands behind your head.
Brace your torso and avoid arching your back or allowing the cable to pull your elbows wide.

dumbbell-overhead-triceps-extension.description: A two-handed overhead extension that moves one dumbbell behind the head and back to straight arms.
instructions: Stand or sit tall, cup both hands around one dumbbell end, and hold it overhead with your elbows aimed forward.
Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head while keeping your upper arms nearly vertical.
Extend your elbows to bring the dumbbell back over your head, then begin the next controlled lowering phase.
Keep your ribs down, maintain a firm two-handed hold, and do not let your elbows flare apart.

single-arm-dumbbell-overhead-extension.description: A one-arm overhead extension that isolates each triceps while the torso maintains a stable position.
instructions: Stand or sit upright and hold one dumbbell overhead with your palm facing inward and elbow close to your head.
Lower the dumbbell behind your shoulder by bending the elbow without letting the upper arm tip sideways.
Straighten the arm above you, then return to the lowered position with control before changing sides.
Keep your head neutral and prevent your ribs, shoulder, or wrist from shifting to assist the lift.

dumbbell-triceps-kickback.description: A hinged dumbbell extension that trains the triceps while the upper arm remains aligned with the torso.
instructions: Take a staggered stance, hinge with a flat back, brace one hand on your front thigh, and hold the dumbbell with your working elbow bent beside your torso.
Extend the elbow to sweep the dumbbell backward while keeping the upper arm fixed in place.
Finish with the arm straight behind you, then bend the elbow slowly until the dumbbell returns beneath it.
Keep your shoulder square to the floor and avoid swinging the dumbbell or lifting the elbow higher to gain momentum.

barbell-skull-crusher.description: A lying barbell extension that trains both triceps as the elbows bend and straighten above the bench.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench, hold the bar with an overhand grip, and position straight arms above your shoulders.
Bend your elbows to lower the bar toward the space just behind your forehead while keeping your upper arms steady.
Extend your elbows to return the bar over your shoulders, stopping with controlled straight arms.
Keep your wrists aligned with your forearms and prevent your elbows from spreading as the bar approaches your head.

dumbbell-skull-crusher.description: A lying triceps extension using separate dumbbells for an independent, neutral-grip arm path.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other, and arms extended above your shoulders.
Bend both elbows to lower the dumbbells beside your temples while your upper arms remain angled upward.
Straighten your elbows to bring the dumbbells back over your shoulders, then lower them again under control.
Keep each wrist firm and each elbow tracking forward so the dumbbells stay clear of your face.

close-grip-bench-press.description: A barbell press with a narrower hand position that emphasizes elbow extension while the chest assists.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench, plant your feet, and grip the racked bar around shoulder width with wrists over forearms.
Unrack the bar and lower it toward your lower chest with your elbows tracking close to your torso.
Press the bar upward until your arms are straight, then stabilize it over your shoulders before the next descent.
Keep your shoulder blades set on the bench and avoid an excessively narrow grip that forces your wrists outward.

machine-triceps-extension.description: A seated machine movement that guides elbow extension while the upper arms stay supported on the pad.
instructions: Adjust the seat so your elbows align with the machine pivot, place your upper arms on the pad, and grasp the handles.
Press the handles through the machine arc by straightening your elbows without lifting your arms from the pad.
Reach the end of the extension smoothly, then let the handles return until your elbows are comfortably bent.
Keep your back against the seat and avoid slamming the lever into either end of its travel.

assisted-dip.description: A machine-supported dip that offsets part of the bodyweight while the triceps drive the pressing motion.
instructions: Set the assistance, grip the parallel handles, and place your knees or feet securely on the moving platform with your torso upright.
Lower the platform under control by bending your elbows and keeping them directed behind you.
Press through the handles until your arms are straight, then settle the platform before beginning another descent.
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears and enter or leave the moving platform only when it is stable.

bench-dip.description: A bodyweight triceps press performed from the edge of a bench with the feet supported on the floor.
instructions: Sit on a stable bench, place your palms on its front edge beside your hips, and walk your feet forward as your hips clear the bench.
Bend your elbows straight behind you to lower your hips close to the bench while keeping your chest upright.
Press the bench away until your arms are straight, then stabilize your hips before lowering again.
Keep your back near the bench and stop the descent before your shoulders roll forward or your elbows flare.

triceps-dip.description: An upright parallel-bar dip that uses bodyweight resistance to emphasize the triceps.
instructions: Mount the parallel bars, support yourself on straight arms, and hold your torso upright with your legs clear of the floor.
Lower your body by bending your elbows behind you while maintaining the upright torso position.
Press down into the bars until your arms are straight, then regain a motionless support before repeating.
Keep your shoulders away from your ears and avoid bouncing out of the bottom or swinging your legs.

weighted-dip.description: A parallel-bar triceps dip performed with a mechanically secured weight plate for added resistance.
instructions: Secure the weight plate with a station-approved loading attachment, mount the parallel bars carefully, and establish an upright straight-arm support.
Descend smoothly by bending your elbows behind you while the secured plate remains quiet beneath your hips.
Drive the bars downward to return to straight arms, pause to stop any sway, and repeat from a stable position.
Confirm the attachment is closed, keep the plate clear of the station, and dismount only after the plate is still.

diamond-push-up.description: A close-hand push-up that places a greater share of the pressing work on the triceps.
instructions: Start in a high plank with your thumbs and index fingers forming a diamond beneath your chest and your body in one line.
Lower your chest toward your hands by bending your elbows back along your sides without letting your hips sag.
Press the floor away until your elbows are straight, then reset the rigid plank before the next repetition.
Keep pressure spread across your palms and adjust the hand spacing if you cannot keep your wrists and elbows aligned.
